channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Neymar? Campanha de gigante do fast food atiça fãs de futebol na internet: ‘nem foi convocado’
item.description: Burger King's 2026 World Cup campaign sparked controversy by indirectly referencing Neymar with the phrase 'he wasn't even called up,' alluding to his absence from the official sticker album. While some praised the ad as humorous and on-brand, others called it disrespectful. A Datafolha poll shows 53% of Brazilians want Neymar selected by Ancelotti despite his recent injuries and limited playing time at Al Hilal.

item.title: Troca de ministros, racha no governo Lula e eleições atrasam plano de transição energética; entenda
item.description: Brazil's energy transition plan, originally set for release on February 6, is delayed due to internal government divisions, recent ministerial changes, and the approaching 2026 elections. The delay undermines the country's ambition to lead global climate agreements, particularly after Lula's commitment at COP30, raising concerns about his international credibility on this priority issue.

item.title: Remoção de agente da PF escala tensão entre Brasil e EUA com ameaça de Lula sobre uso de reciprocidade
item.description: The U.S. government demanded the removal of a Brazilian Federal Police agent who worked with ICE, escalating tensions between the two countries. During a visit to Germany, President Lula mentioned the possibility of adopting reciprocal measures against the U.S. The incident adds to recent disputes, including trade tensions and Washington’s intention to label Brazilian criminal factions as terrorists, alongside the release of Alexandre Ramagem after his arrest in Miami.

item.title: Galipolo vive maior pressão à frente do Banco Central; ‘Traidor’, diz líder do PT na Câmara
item.description: Banco Central President Gabriel Galípolo faces political pressure from the PT and Lula's government after stating that internal investigations found no fault by his predecessor, Roberto Campos Neto, in the Banco Master scandal. PT leaders, including Pedro Uczai, have called him a 'traitor', as the government seeks to tie the scandal to Bolsonaro's administration for electoral gain. Tensions are rising six months ahead of the 2026 election, with Galípolo maintaining his stance despite political pressure.

item.title: CCJ remarca sabatina de Jorge Messias para 29 de abril
item.description: The Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee rescheduled the hearing of Attorney General Jorge Messias for April 29, 2026, after an earlier move to April 28 was reversed due to quorum concerns. Messias currently has 13 favorable and 8 opposing votes in the committee, needing one more vote for majority approval. If cleared, his nomination will proceed to a secret Senate floor vote requiring at least 41 votes for Supreme Court appointment.

item.title: Todos pintados para a guerra eleitoral
item.description: The 2026 presidential campaign has officially opened with intensified electoral actions, driven by a technical tie between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in opinion polls. The PT accuses the government of favoring Flávio Bolsonaro due to his surname and a crafted image of moderation, without voters knowing his real attributes. The Lula campaign aims to expose who is being positioned as Jair Bolsonaro’s chosen successor in the electronic ballot.

item.title: Ana Paula Renault leva prêmio recorde de R$ 5,7 milhões do “BBB”
item.description: Ana Paula Renault, 44, won BBB 2026 with 75.94% of the votes and took home a record prize of R$ 5.7 million, the highest in the show's history. Her victory was celebrated by politicians such as Duda Salabert (Psol-MG) and Rogério Correia (PT-MG), who praised her courage and symbolic significance for Brazilians. Despite the death of her father, Gerardo Renault, at 96, she chose to remain in the competition.

item.title: Sem priorizar competições, Flamengo inicia na Copa do Brasil contra o Vitória e aposta na capacidade de Jardim de rodar o time
item.description: Flamengo begins its 2026 Copa do Brasil campaign against Vitória at Maracanã, avoiding explicit prioritization of any competition and relying on squad depth to compete across three fronts. Coach Leonardo Jardim has rotated the lineup due to injuries and suspensions, repeating the starting XI only once in 11 matches, and will rely on the return of Saúl and possibly Jorginho, while Paquetá, Pulgar, and Carrascal remain sidelined.

item.title: Flávio planeja reajustar aposentadorias e despesas com saúde e educação só pela inflação
item.description: The economic team of pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) states that a fiscal adjustment of two percentage points of GDP would be politically viable if he is elected. The plan proposes adjusting pensions and spending on health and education solely by inflation to control public expenditures.

item.title: Autofagia constitucional
item.description: The article examines the growing influence of the Brazilian Supreme Federal Court (STF) in national politics, arguing that its actions may be overstepping constitutional boundaries and encroaching on domains reserved for elected officials. While this judicial prominence reflects democratic consolidation, it risks undermining the legitimacy of popular votes and turning constitutional defense into a tool for weakening institutional politics. The text warns of 'constitutional self-devouring,' where the guardian of democracy erodes the very foundations that sustain it.

item.title: São Paulo desfigura Lei Cidade Limpa em pastiche da Times Square
item.description: São Paulo authorities are planning to amend the 2006 Cidade Limpa Law to install massive LED panels on Avenida São João, covering up to 70% of historic building facades and reaching 25 meters in height, in a project dubbed the 'Paulistana Times Square'. Despite warnings from the Brazilian Architects Institute, urbanist Mauro Calliari, and CET regarding heritage defacement, renewed visual pollution, and road safety risks, the project was approved by municipal councils under the justification of revitalizing the downtown area and attracting investment.

item.title: Ampliação do Minha Casa Minha Vida começa a valer: financiamento para quem ganha até R$ 13 mil e imóveis de até R$ 600 mil
item.description: The federal government has expanded the Minha Casa Minha Vida program to include families earning up to R$13,000 and properties valued at up to R$600,000, standardizing interest rates at 0.99%. An additional R$20 billion from the Pré-Sal Social Fund will support the construction of one million housing units this year, alongside raising the renovation subsidy cap to R$50,000 and extending the repayment term to 72 months.

item.title: Comissão da Câmara retoma votação da PEC do fim da escala 6x1 nesta quarta-feira
item.description: The Chamber's Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) resumes voting on Wednesday on the PEC to end the 6x1 work schedule, with rapporteur Deputy Paulo Azi (União Brasil-BA) affirming its constitutionality and advocating for a transition period and productive sector compensation. The proposal aims for a 40-hour workweek and a 5x2 schedule, amid government pressure from Lula's administration, which has submitted its own constitutional urgency bill. If approved, a special committee will be formed to discuss the bill's merits before a plenary vote.

item.title: STF tem 3 votos para condenar Eduardo Bolsonaro por difamação contra Tabata
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court has formed three votes to convict former deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro (PL) of defamation against federal deputy Tabata Amaral (PSB-SP), with rapporteur Alexandre de Moraes supported by ministers Flávio Dino and Cármen Lúcia, proposing one year of detention in semi-open regime for 2021 social media posts implying illegitimate ties between the deputy and business interests.

item.title: Zema publica vídeo humorístico com críticas a Gilmar Mendes
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo), a pre-candidate for President, shared a 2018 humorous video from Porta dos Fundos that satirizes Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes, one day after Mendes requested Zema's inclusion in the fake news inquiry for allegedly disparaging the Court's honor. Zema responded with irony, stating that if the goal is to jail all who criticize the 'untouchables', then 'jailing the whole of Brazil' would be necessary. The video, modeled after Ipiranga gas station ads, portrays the STF as a 'gas station' where all judicial decisions — from habeas corpus to suspending evidence against politicians — are resolved by Gilmar Mendes, referencing Zema's 'Os Intocáveis' series that uses deepfake to mimic ministers' voices.

item.title: Tadeu Alencar deixa cargo de ministro do Empreendedorismo e aponta ‘tensões indesejadas’ no PSB
item.description: Tadeu Alencar resigned as Minister of Entrepreneurship, Microbusiness and Small Business Enterprise just 18 days after his appointment, citing 'undesired tensions' within the PSB. He emphasized he did not actively seek the position and that his departure aims to preserve government and party unity, despite honoring the opportunity to serve. Alencar stepped down with his head held high, thanking Lula and reaffirming his commitment to Brazil's national reconstruction project.

item.title: Saiba quem é Paulo Henrique Pereira, novo ministro do Empreendedorismo
item.description: Paulo Henrique Pereira, a law professor at USP and PSB member, was appointed Minister of Entrepreneurship by acting president Geraldo Alckmin, replacing Tadeu Alencar, who served only 18 days. Pereira previously served as national secretary of Justice at MJSP, executive secretary of the Sustainable Economic and Social Development Council, and national consumer secretary in the Lula government. The change followed a PSB reorganization request, with party leader João Campos endorsing Pereira to avoid internal party tensions.

item.title: A crise na Polícia Militar de São Paulo está no retrovisor de Guilherme Derrite
item.description: The family of medical student Marco Aurélio, killed by an off-duty military police officer in 2024 after tapping a patrol car's side mirror, was only heard by state security officials after a year and a half of waiting. The case reveals a pattern of institutional violence within São Paulo's Military Police under Guilherme Derrite's leadership, accused of politicizing the force, undermining hierarchy, promoting allies from the Rota unit, and failing to investigate corruption and PCC-linked crimes. Colonels warn that partisan politics has invaded the barracks, eroding command and control.

item.title: CCJ do Senado volta atrás e sabatina de Jorge Messias deve acontecer dia 29 de abril
item.description: The Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) rescheduled the hearing for Jorge Messias, Lula's nominee to the Supreme Court, to April 29, after initially moving it to April 28 due to concerns about proximity to Labor Day. The change was reversed because of senators' difficulty attending early Tuesday hearings. Relator Weverton Rocha issued a favorable report. Messias, current Attorney General of the Union, requires an absolute majority in the Senate for approval.

item.title: Flávio Dino propõe uma nova reforma do Judiciário
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino proposed a new judicial reform focused on legal security, access to rights, and efficiency. The proposal includes 15 axes, such as revising the penal code for corruption involving public officials, ending punitive compulsory retirement, and ensuring proper proceedings in Electoral Justice. Dino emphasized the reform requires legislative changes and was praised by STF President Edson Fachin for addressing societal demands for transparency and public trust in institutions.

item.title: STF tem 3 votos para condenar Eduardo Bolsonaro a um ano de detenção por difamar Tabata Amaral
item.description: The Brazilian Supreme Court (STF) has three votes to convict Eduardo Bolsonaro to one year of detention in an open regime for defaming federal deputy Tabata Amaral, after he suggested her bill on public distribution of sanitary pads illicitly benefited third parties. Justices Alexandre de Moraes, Cármen Lúcia, and Flávio Dino voted for conviction, emphasizing Bolsonaro’s awareness of the offensive nature of his posts. Seven more justices remain to vote in the virtual plenary.

item.title: Lula fala em adotar reciprocidade à ação do governo americano contra delegado da PF
item.description: President Lula said he may adopt reciprocity in response to the U.S. government's action, which requested a Brazilian Federal Police delegate leave the country after involvement in the arrest of former congressman Alexandre Ramagem. Delegate Marcelo Ivo de Carvalho, an ICE liaison officer, was already returning to Brazil, and the Brazilian government dismissed the allegations as unfounded, emphasizing his work was based on bilateral cooperation agreements.

item.title: Lula: esquerda também tem de aprender a lidar com novos anseios do trabalhador
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said the Brazilian left must learn to address workers’ new aspirations following changes in labor relations. He made the comment during an interview with the podcast Calma Urgente! while in Barcelona on a trip to Europe.

item.title: Dino dá 3º voto para condenar Eduardo Bolsonaro por difamação contra Tabata
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino voted to condemn Eduardo Bolsonaro for defamation against Congresswoman Tabata Amaral, following the rapporteur Alexandre de Moraes. This marks the third vote in favor of holding the former deputy accountable, after Justice Cármen Lúcia had already supported Moraes on Monday. The case stems from allegations that Bolsonaro publicly defamed Tabata.

item.title: Presidente Lula encerra viagem de cinco dias à Europa
item.description: President Lula concluded his five-day trip to Europe with a brief visit to Portugal, where he met with Prime Minister Luís Montenegro and President António José Seguro. The discussions focused on economic cooperation, immigration, and the progress of the Mercosul-European Union agreement, with Lula emphasizing the strengthening of bilateral ties and asserting that the deal will expand investment opportunities between Brazil and Portugal.

item.title: Sabatina de Messias volta a ser reagendada para o dia 29
item.description: The sabatina of Jorge Messias, nominated by President Lula for a vacancy on the STF, was rescheduled to March 29 after being initially set for March 28. Otto Alencar, president of the Senate's CCJ, explained the change was made to accommodate senators who arrive later in Brasília on Wednesdays. The vote in both the CCJ and plenary is expected to occur on the same day, with Messias needing at least 13 votes in the committee and 41 in the full Senate for approval.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro acusa cúpula da PF de agir como “gestapo”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) accused the leadership of the Federal Police of acting like a 'gestapo', claiming agents were operating illegally in the shadows to persecute government opponents abroad. The statement was made on Tuesday, the 21st, in an interview with O Antagonista.

item.title: Itamaraty se reúne com EUA após expulsão de delegado e Lula fala em reciprocidade
item.description: The Itamaraty met with the U.S. Embassy's Chargé d'Affaires, Kimberly Kelly, to discuss the expulsion of Brazilian Federal Police delegate Marcelo Ivo, following U.S. allegations of immigration system manipulation and political persecution. Brazil signaled potential reciprocity, with Lula stating that U.S. agents could be expelled from Brazil in response, though the final decision awaits his return from Europe.

item.title: Governador de Minas diz ter “inveja branca” de Tarcísio
item.description: Minas Gerais Governor Mateus Simões (PSD) said he felt 'white envy' toward São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) for appointing the first woman as commander-general of the São Paulo Military Police, a phrase deemed racist. The comment was made during the Medalha da Inconfidência ceremony in Ouro Preto, where Tarcísio received the state’s highest honor. Simões noted that Minas Gerais already has a female military commander, Colonel Jordana Filgueiras Daldegan, who leads the state’s fire brigade.

item.title: Lula enfatiza que dados bons de inflação e emprego ainda são pouco para o povo
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva emphasized that despite positive indicators in inflation and employment, the population does not yet perceive tangible improvements in their daily lives. He stressed that good macroeconomic data are insufficient if they do not translate into income, access to services, and dignity for the people. The statement reflects a critique of the disconnect between official statistics and the lived reality of Brazilians.

item.title: Itamaraty se reúne com Embaixada dos EUA para tratar de expulsão de delegado e fala em reciprocidade
item.description: Brazil's foreign ministry met with the U.S. Embassy to discuss the expulsion of Federal Police delegate Marcelo Ivo, with officials warning of potential reciprocity. President Lula stated Brazil may expel U.S. agents in response to what he views as U.S. overreach, following the arrest of former deputy Alexandre Ramagem on a traffic violation despite his conviction for attempted coup by the STF.

item.title: STF tem 3 a 0 para condenar Eduardo Bolsonaro a indenizar Tabata
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court's 1st Chamber formed a 3-0 majority to convict former congressman Eduardo Bolsonaro of defamation against federal deputy Tabata Amaral, with votes from Alexandre de Moraes (relator), Cármen Lúcia, and Flávio Dino. The conviction stems from an October 2021 video falsely linking Tabata to businessman Jorge Paulo Lemann and P&G, implying a conflict of interest in her bill to distribute sanitary pads in schools. The proposed sentence includes one year of detention in an open initial regime and a fine of R$ 85.800, equivalent to 39 day-fines.

item.title: Flávio Dino dá terceiro voto para condenar Eduardo Bolsonaro por difamação contra Tabata
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino voted to condemn Eduardo Bolsonaro for defamation against Deputy Tabata Amaral, after he shared false content on social media claiming she proposed a sanitary pad law to benefit Jorge Paulo Lemann. With Dino’s vote, the tally is 3-0 in favor of conviction, with seven justices still to vote. The rapporteur, Alexandre de Moraes, set a penalty of one year in open regime detention and 39 day-fines, equivalent to about R$126,400.

item.title: Representante dos EUA é convocada a dar explicações ao governo brasileiro sobre pedido para que delegado da PF deixe EUA
item.description: The U.S. government requested that Brazilian Federal Police delegate Marcelo Ivo de Carvalho, who worked with ICE, leave the country, prompting Brazilian protest. The U.S. Chargé d'Affaires in Brasília, Kimberly Kelly, was summoned by Brazil's Foreign Ministry for clarification. President Lula and Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira indicated possible reciprocity and await official explanations.

item.title: ELEIÇÕES 2026: Flávio Bolsonaro ironiza Lula e convoca jovens a tirar título de eleitor
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro used a YouTube live stream to mock President Lula and urge young people to register to vote, aiming to mobilize the conservative base ahead of the 2026 elections. Despite technical interruptions in the video, the broadcast reinforced opposition rhetoric and highlighted digital engagement as a key political strategy.

item.title: Copa do Brasil: Alex Telles marca no fim e Botafogo vence Chapecoense
item.description: Botafogo defeated Chapecoense 1-0 in the first leg of the Copa do Brasil round of 16, with Alex Telles scoring in stoppage time. Despite numerous chances throughout the match, Botafogo struggled to break down Chapecoense's defense until the late goal secured the victory.

item.title: Em SP, líder evangélico sinaliza apoio à pré-candidatura de Ronaldo Caiado ao Planalto
item.description: Former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado received a signal of support from evangelical leader Apostle César Augusto during an event in São Paulo, who praised his courage and experience to lead the country. Caiado used the occasion to reinforce his political trajectory and implicitly contrast himself with Flávio Bolsonaro, emphasizing his record in Goiás where 'criminals do not grow'. The event is part of Caiado’s strategy to engage evangelical voters, following prior meetings with leaders of the Assembleia de Deus Ministério Madureira.

item.title: Zema pede coragem contra “intocáveis” do STF em cerimônia da Inconfidência
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo), a pre-candidate for president, criticized the STF during the Inconfidência Medal ceremony in Ouro Preto, accusing ministers of being 'untouchables' and perpetuating a 'colonial cycle' in Brasília. He referenced alleged scandals involving lawyer Viviane de Moraes (wife of Justice Alexandre de Moraes) and Banco Master, and criticized Justice Gilmar Mendes for seeking inclusion in the fake news inquiry. Zema also praised São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas for governing seriously and without cheap populism.

item.title: ‘Sou um cara de jogo de cintura, mas não chego ao teatro rebolado’, diz Wagner sobre críticas ao STF
item.description: Senator Jaques Wagner (PT-BA), government leader in the Senate, says he will not collaborate in attacks on the Supreme Federal Court (STF), even when they come from his own party, stating he’d rather not return to office if he has to 'come back disguised'. Although he supported a 2023 PEC to limit individual STF rulings, he criticizes the 'frenzy' of attacking the Court and notes that political timing differs from the justices’ sphere, which he describes as 'another bubble'. Wagner, running for re-election in 2026, spoke during the PT’s 8th Congress, where a code of ethics for the STF is being debated, following the Banco Master scandal that strained Lula’s relationship with the Court.

item.title: “Nós nos tornamos o sistema”, diz Lula sobre esquerda
item.description: President Lula (PT) criticized the left for becoming part of the 'system' by prioritizing governability over public policies, which he views as a betrayal of popular trust. He argued this shift has opened space for anti-system discourses and weakened the left's identity.

item.title: A criminalização do dissenso vai se tornando regra e não é um bom prenúncio para o ano eleitoral
item.description: Fernando Schüler criticizes the criminalization of dissent in Brazil, noting that the inclusion of former governor Romeu Zema in the fake news inquiry over a political satire sets a dangerous precedent for freedom of expression. He contrasts current repression with historical tolerance by figures like Emperor Pedro II, José Sarney, and Fernando Henrique Cardoso, who accepted criticism and satire as democratic norms. Schüler argues that this pattern, beginning in 2019 with the fake news investigation, now threatens opposition candidates like Flávio Bolsonaro with potential ineligibility and signals a troubling outlook for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Lula defende acordo UE-Mercosul e propõe Portugal como porta de entrada para empresas brasileiras
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defended the Mercosul-European Union agreement during a visit to Lisbon and proposed Portugal as a gateway for Brazilian companies into the European market. He praised globalization and emphasized the importance of international cooperation for Brazil's economic development.

item.title: Nikolas posta meme após nova cobrança de apoio a Flávio
item.description: Federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) posted a meme on X after being criticized by Bolsonarists for allegedly lacking support for Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL-RJ) presidential bid. According to Folha de S.Paulo, he mentioned Flávio in only 10 of his 544 posts on the platform. The meme served as an indirect response to loyalty pressures within the Bolsonarist base.

item.title: Tarcísio: “Talvez gastemos muita energia com polarização que não nos leva a nada”
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas criticized Brazil's political polarization during a speech in Ouro Preto (MG) while receiving the Great Collar of the Inconfidência Mineira. Without directly naming President Lula, he suggested the country may be wasting excessive energy on conflicts that lead to no productive outcomes.

item.title: Lula sopesa aplicar “la reciprocidad” a Estados Unidos tras la expulsión de un enlace policial brasileño en Florida
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva condemned the expulsion of a Brazilian police liaison by U.S. authorities, stating Brazil will respond in kind under the principle of reciprocity. He accused the U.S. government of abusing its power and renewed his criticism of former President Donald Trump, citing growing tensions in bilateral relations amid delays in a planned meeting and the proximity of a closely contested U.S. election.

item.title: Tarcísio recebe medalha em MG e critica polarização no país
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas received the Great Collar of the Inconfidência in Ouro Preto (MG) and criticized political polarization in Brazil, questioning whether the heroes of the Inconfidência Mineira would be satisfied with the country's current state. He also praised former Minas Gerais Governor Romeu Zema for his fiscally responsible administration.

item.title: Lula ironiza Trump: ‘É importante que a gente dê logo o Prêmio Nobel da Paz’
item.description: President Lula ironically suggested that Donald Trump should immediately receive the Nobel Peace Prize after Trump claimed to have ended eight wars without being awarded it. The remark was made in Lisbon during Lula’s European tour, where he lamented the lack of any institution capable of fostering global peace.

item.title: Oposição articula novo pedido de impeachment de Gilmar Mendes após pedido para incluir Zema no inquérito das fake news
item.description: Opposition lawmakers announced a new impeachment request against Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes after he sought to include former Minas Gerais Governor Romeu Zema in the fake news inquiry over a satirical video. The opposition argues the move criminalizes institutional criticism and threatens free speech, calling it a dangerous precedent for democracy.

item.title: Zema compara ministros do STF a coroa portuguesa em vídeo sobre inconfidência mineira
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo-MG), a pre-candidate for president, compared STF ministers to the Portuguese crown in a social media video, stating that 'in place of the Portuguese crown sit the untouchables of Brasília'. The remark was made in reference to the Inconfidência Mineira, a historical movement resisting central authority.

item.title: Carlos Bolsonaro anuncia 'levantamento' de prefeitos e vereadores do PL que 'não divulgam' a candidatura de Flávio
item.description: Carlos Bolsonaro announced he will conduct a survey of PL mayors and council members who are not publicizing his brother Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign, aiming to correct their stance through party leadership. He criticized the lack of political expression and urged supporters to respectfully expose omissions by fellow party members. The move reflects growing internal divisions within the Brazilian right, including recent clashes with Eduardo and Nikolas Bolsonaro.
